spectrum.verdict: not consistent with ultracool dwarf templates
warmer than M8: probably an ordinary star
spectrum.doubt: its 1.4 micrometre water band is shallower than a M8's

plain: We could not follow it from year to year: in single WISE epochs it is too faint or sits on other stars, so its motion is not measured here. Stacking all WISE images along its catalog motion (0.35 arcseconds per year) does show it (signal-to-noise 31), so it is there, just too faint to follow year by year.
Its infrared colour W1-W2 = 0.95 mag is red, as for early-T and the reddest L brown dwarfs (dusty or very cool stars can look like this too).
Its infrared brightness stays constant within the measurement errors.
Its SPHEREx spectrum is closest to one of the warmest templates (M8), but its 1.4 micrometre water band is shallower than a M8's: probably an ordinary star, warmer than the ultracool dwarfs.
